A lexicon of looks. In your nameless gaze was spoken all that could be lost or gained. In my paralysis, between my desire to be beckoned and my harping fear, I came to hold the intimate aloneness of the one without need. So as you departed, in the emptiness of our inscrutable yearnings, you taught me the roads and ways, glorious without miles, that lead to the bridal chamber, where in repose fastidious being is at one with all it could ever care to love. You taught me in your leaving, for as you traveled the country roads, I walked your way, with peace found nowhere in particular, uncanny and resplendent. And yet I see your image in mind, fragments in recollection of a mocking wish who's provenance is the pain of a dreamed division. I no longer long for you, dream for you, and I'm not sure I ever truly did. Now that the furor of your features has made off with me, I grant you this gratitude, for you showed me that the heart of longing dies gladly to feel its own pulse, and now my heart jumps in my hand as I am graced with the recollection of that which I've always had, but yet never quite held. Now I know why I couldn't bring myself to say hi. Now you repeat for me as the history of my longing unwinds and opens out, as you now take the nominal position of the promise of togetherness. But it's dawning on me that no position is fit to clarify the true state for my passions; indeed love must know itself on all levels, and that die is cast in flesh and blood which paints matrimony upon the canvas of my wishing. So I in all honesty am glad you had to go, and will let the heart ruminate on the mystery of futures fated by the magnetism of kindred souls. I will bear the sense of loss and regret because they are my teachers; I will bear the aching for those unread chapters, in which you still may play a part in this hearts story; I will garner no fantasy on behalf of my need; and I will let run free all fantasy which may by a hand divine sculpt circumstance to yet bring what is true to the threshold of my living love. The waves of longing crash, and inevitably are drawn back into the sea. As they recede they make patterns upon the sands of my memory and remind me that some part of me wishes the longings to represent something real and true, but as the tide draws out, it becomes clear that even that meaning is an attempt by a fragment, limited to its imaginings and conceits, to find something whole and eternal, which I feel, in this case, is a doleful misgiving. But when the waves come again, and who knows if they will, I will be here to wonder at their significance, and awash I'll bask, grateful for their cleansing spirit, in embrace with the story of love's caroming, vertiginous con-tending.
